content:
Scientific Concept: Standard Model of Particle Physics
Domain: particles / high_energy_physics
Definition: Gauge quantum field theory based on SU(3)_C x SU(2)_L x U(1)_Y gauge symmetry group classifying all known elementary subatomic particles and their fundamental interactions.

Principles:
Matter Constituents: 12 fundamental fermions (6 quarks: u, d, c, s, t, b; 6 leptons: e, mu, tau, nu_e, nu_mu, nu_tau).
Gauge Bosons (Force Carriers): Photon (electromagnetic), 8 Gluons (strong), W+, W-, Z0 (weak force).
Scalar Boson: Higgs boson (H0) responsible for electroweak symmetry breaking and giving mass to gauge bosons and charged fermions.
Antimatter: Every particle has a corresponding antiparticle with opposite electric charge and quantum numbers (e.g. positron e+).

Experimental Proofs:
Discovery of neutral currents at CERN Gargamelle bubble chamber (1973)
Discovery of W and Z bosons at CERN UA1/UA2 experiments (1983)
Discovery of Top quark at Fermilab Tevatron (1995)
Observation of Higgs boson at CERN Large Hadron Collider (ATLAS & CMS, 2012)

Applications:
Positron Emission Tomography (PET medical imaging)
Semiconductor radiation hardening
Superconducting magnet technology
